## Historical audit: S0006

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_96943062/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file; observations were supplied whole, not split.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal: student request, line 1 | Reconstruct a 384 × 512 indoor photograph with separate meshes and matching camera, framing and materials, without using the image as a texture. The student’s “damaged classroom” interpretation is an inferred scene identity, not independent evidence of the image’s contents. |
| Initial build: student response and execution, lines 3–4 | Code specifies multiple objects: room shell, windows, ceiling grid, board, flag, wall fixtures, debris and overlapping yellow panels. It positions board frames, flag parts and tilted debris separately; their actual connections, contacts and poses are not geometrically verified. It attempts rough materials and procedural carpet/plaster texture, plus camera, lights and Cycles settings. |
| Failure and feedback: execution result and student request, lines 5–6 | Step 1 failed because `sc.world` was `None` at the color assignment; no image was returned. The student received the traceback and a request to revise. This is runtime feedback, not teacher diagnosis or advice. |
| Revision and validation: student response, execution and result, lines 8–10 | The student created a world if absent, changed camera and lighting, lengthened/repositioned the board and moved debris and panels. Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file; the log shows 16 samples despite code requesting 48. Step 2 was selected (line 11). This establishes execution success, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Review and unexecuted proposal: student request/session/response, lines 12–14 | The reference and step-2 render were supplied for review, with zero executions remaining. The student returned another complete program rather than `DONE`: it proposed further room, camera, lighting, material and object-position changes, including color-based material identification. No execution or selection of that program is visible. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher event, diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or evidence of teacher input or adoption appears in this student trajectory. The student independently produced and revised code in response to runner feedback; the recorded sessions show zero tool calls (lines 2, 7, 13). The first revision preceded any successful render, so its scene adjustments cannot be attributed to rendered-image inspection.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** A technical failure was followed by a successful rendered build and formal selection of step 2. Overall reconstruction quality is **unknown**, not established success or partial correctness: the supplied audit contains image paths, not inspectable image pixels or an independent visual assessment. Consequently, camera/framing, illumination, texture application, object occlusion, pose and part connection remain unresolved. The final proposed revision is not the selected or visibly executed build.

**Transferable lesson:** distinguish runtime success from scene fidelity, and verify world initialization before assigning world properties. **Task-specific hypotheses:** the altered camera, board and debris layout might better match the photograph, and generic Blender object names might have prevented name-based texture targeting; neither improvement is validated here.
